From e04ed278d25bf15769800bf6e35c6737f137186f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jackie Liu <liuyun01@kylinos.cn>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 18:15:53 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] mm/damon/stat: fix memory leak on damon_start() failure in
 damon_stat_start()

Destroy the DAMON context and reset the global pointer when damon_start()
fails.  Otherwise, the context allocated by damon_stat_build_ctx() is
leaked, and the stale damon_stat_context pointer will be overwritten on
the next enable attempt, making the old allocation permanently
unreachable.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/20260331101553.88422-1-liu.yun@linux.dev
Fixes: 369c415e6073 ("mm/damon: introduce DAMON_STAT module")
Signed-off-by: Jackie Liu <liuyun01@kylinos.cn>
Reviewed-by: SeongJae Park <sj@kernel.org>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 6.17.x
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/mm/damon/stat.c b/mm/damon/stat.c
index cf2c5a541eee..5a742fc157e4 100644
--- a/mm/damon/stat.c
+++ b/mm/damon/stat.c
@@ -249,8 +249,11 @@ static int damon_stat_start(void)
 	if (!damon_stat_context)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 	err = damon_start(&damon_stat_context, 1, true);
-	if (err)
+	if (err) {
+		damon_destroy_ctx(damon_stat_context);
+		damon_stat_context = NULL;
 		return err;
+	}
 
 	damon_stat_last_refresh_jiffies = jiffies;
 	call_control.data = damon_stat_context;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

### Modifications in Each File

**`mm/damon/stat.c`**  
- In the `damon_stat_start()` function, added error handling after the call to `damon_start()`.  
- If `damon_start()` returns an error, the patch now:  
  1. Destroys the DAMON context via `damon_destroy_ctx(damon_stat_context)`.  
  2. Resets the global pointer `damon_stat_context` to `NULL`.  
- Previously, failure of `damon_start()` would cause the function to return the error immediately without cleaning up the context, leading to a memory leak.

### Relationships Among Modifications

The only modified file is `mm/damon/stat.c`, and the changes are confined to a single function (`damon_stat_start`). The relationship is causal:  

- The context allocated by `damon_stat_build_ctx()` at the beginning of the function must be freed if the subsequent `damon_start()` call fails.  
- Without the fix, the allocated context would be leaked (no reference to it after returning the error), and the stale `damon_stat_context` pointer would be overwritten on the next enable attempt, making the old allocation permanently unreachable.  
- The fix ensures proper resource cleanup and prevents both a memory leak and the stale-pointer problem.

Here is the commit message:
mm/damon/stat: fix memory leak on damon_start() failure in
 damon_stat_start()

Destroy the DAMON context and reset the global pointer when damon_start()
fails.  Otherwise, the context allocated by damon_stat_build_ctx() is
leaked, and the stale damon_stat_context pointer will be overwritten on
the next enable attempt, making the old allocation permanently
unreachable.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/20260331101553.88422-1-liu.yun@linux.dev
Fixes: 369c415e6073 ("mm/damon: introduce DAMON_STAT module")
Signed-off-by: Jackie Liu <liuyun01@kylinos.cn>
Reviewed-by: SeongJae Park <sj@kernel.org>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 6.17.x
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
In damon_stat_start(), after allocating a DAMON context via damon_stat_build_ctx() and assigning it to the global pointer damon_stat_context, the subsequent call to damon_start() may fail. The original code returned the error immediately without destroying the context or resetting the global pointer, causing a memory leak (the allocated context is never freed) and leaving a stale pointer that will be overwritten on the next enable attempt, making the old allocation permanently unreachable.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int damon_stat_start(void)
 {
 	int err;
 
 	damon_stat_context = damon_stat_build_ctx();
 	if (!damon_stat_context)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 	err = damon_start(&damon_stat_context, 1, true);
-	if (err)
+	if (err) {
+		damon_destroy_ctx(damon_stat_context);
+		damon_stat_context = NULL;
 		return err;
+	}
 
 	damon_stat_last_refresh_jiffies = jiffies;
 	call_control.data = damon_stat_context;
 	return damon_call(damon_stat_context, &call_control);
 }
